problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the municipal budget across 9 different infrastructure projects to maximize the total projected benefit to the community. The characteristics of each project are as follows:
* Project A: projected benefit is 0.092, implementation complexity is 0.207, budget share limits [0.051, 0.497]
* Project B: projected benefit is 0.123, implementation complexity is 0.044, budget share limits [0.050, 0.668]
* Project C: projected benefit is 0.055, implementation complexity is 0.293, budget share limits [0.005, 0.398]
* Project D: projected benefit is 0.120, implementation complexity is 0.124, budget share limits [0.014, 0.894]
* Project E: projected benefit is 0.033, implementation complexity is 0.241, budget share limits [0.033, 0.744]
* Project F: projected benefit is 0.111, implementation complexity is 0.108, budget share limits [0.047, 0.480]
* Project G: projected benefit is 0.158, implementation complexity is 0.282, budget share limits [0.046, 0.502]
* Project H: projected benefit is 0.070, implementation complexity is 0.229, budget share limits [0.061, 0.797]
* Project I: projected benefit is 0.198, implementation complexity is 0.068, budget share limits [0.052, 0.619]

Each project must receive a portion of the total budget that falls within its specified minimum and maximum allocation limits, and the sum of all budget allocations must equal the entire budget. To ensure timely completion, the planner requires that the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by the subset L = {H}, collectively receive at least 0.306 of the total funding. At the same time, the overall implementation complexity of the portfolio, measured by a composite complexity index, must not exceed 0.272, and the total projected benefit of the portfolio must be no less than 0.087. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes total projected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
